query: Is nuclear power the fastest path to decarbonization?

results.title: Nuclear Power and Secure Energy Transitions — IEA
results.snippet: Lifetime extensions of existing reactors are among the cheapest sources of additional low-emissions electricity; net-zero pathways roughly double global nuclear capacity by 2050.

results.title: Nuclear Energy and Climate Change — World Nuclear Association
results.snippet: Nuclear plants deliver large volumes of firm low-carbon power; France's 1974–1989 build-out remains the fastest national decarbonization of an electricity system on record.

results.title: Levelized Cost of Energy+ — Lazard
results.snippet: Unsubsidized utility-scale solar and onshore wind remain the cheapest new-build generation on a levelized basis, while new nuclear carries the highest LCOE range and the widest uncertainty band.

results.title: Nuclear Energy — Our World in Data
results.snippet: Annual additions of solar and wind now far outpace nuclear, though nuclear's 1980s build rates remain unmatched per unit of firm capacity added.

results.title: Projected Costs of Generating Electricity 2020 — OECD NEA
results.snippet: Plant-level LCOE comparisons omit system costs; including balancing and network costs changes the ranking of low-carbon portfolios.

results.title: Nuclear power debate — Wikipedia
results.snippet: Overview of arguments over cost, construction timelines, safety, waste, and the role of nuclear power in climate change mitigation.
